https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

message.content:
I don’t have live access to a movie‑showtime database, so I can’t pull the current schedule for you.  
What I can do is point you toward the best places to look and give you a quick checklist so you’ll find a film that meets your two‑hour limit and is close enough to Times Square that you can walk there.

---

## 1️⃣  Where to start – the nearest theatres

| Theatre | Address | Distance from Times Square |
|---------|---------|----------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** | 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.3 mi (≈10‑12 min walk) |
| **Regal Union Square** | 200 W 14th St, New York, NY 10011 | ~0.8 mi (≈15‑20 min walk) |
| **Regal Midtown 9** | 151 W 45th St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.4 mi (≈12‑15 min walk) |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** | 150 W 34th St, New York, NY 10001 | ~0.7 mi (≈15‑18 min walk) |
| **Theater District’s “Movie” venues** (e.g., Alamo Drafthouse, AMC, Regal) | All around 42nd‑48th Streets & Broadway | 0.2–0.5 mi |

> *Tip:* AMC Empire 25 is the closest and has the most screens, so it’s usually the easiest place to find a short film.

---

## 2️⃣  How to find a < 2‑hour movie

| Step | What to do | Why it matters |
|------|------------|----------------|
| **Check the theatre’s website** | Go to the official site (e.g., `www.amc.com`, `www.regmovies.com`) and click “Showtimes.” | Most sites let you filter by “Duration” or “Runtime.” |
| **Use a third‑party aggregator** | Sites like Fandango, Flixster, or IMDb’s “Now Showing” pages often list runtimes next to each title. | They’re handy if the theatre’s own site doesn’t show runtimes. |
| **Look at the “Shorts” section** | Some theatres have a dedicated “Short Film” or “Indie” program; those are almost always under 90 minutes. | Great for a quick watch. |
| **Read the synopsis** | Even if the runtime isn’t listed, the plot summary will hint at whether it’s a feature-length or a short. | Helps avoid surprises. |
| **Ask the box office** | Call or chat with the theatre staff; they can tell you which films are < 120 min. | Quick confirmation if you’re on the fence. |

---

## 3️⃣  Sample titles that usually run ≤ 2 hours (check current status)

| Title | Approx. Runtime | Notes |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| **“The Grand Budapest Hotel”** | 99 min | Classic comedy‑drama; often shown in repertory cinemas. |
| **“Moonlight”** | 111 min | Oscar‑winning drama; check indie theatres. |
| **“Lady Bird”** | 94 min | Coming‑of‑age story; popular in art‑house venues. |
| **“Parasite”** | 132 min | Slightly over 2 hrs—watch the runtime carefully. |
| **“The Social Network”** | 135 min | Over 2 hrs; skip if strict. |
| **“Shorts” programs** | 5–30 min each | Usually a collection of shorts; great for a quick stop. |

> *Remember:* These runtimes are approximate; always double‑check the exact length on the theatre’s site before buying tickets.

---

## 4️⃣  Practical tips for a smooth outing

| Tip | Why it helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Buy tickets online** | Saves time at the box office and guarantees you a seat. |
| **Arrive early** | Gives you a chance to grab snacks, explore the lobby, and settle in. |
| **Bring a light snack** | Many theatres allow small items; it saves a trip to the concession stand. |
| **Plan a post‑movie walk** | After the film, you can stroll down 7th Avenue or explore Bryant Park. |

---

### Bottom line

1. Pick one of the nearby theatres (AMC Empire 25 is the quickest option).  
2. Visit its website or a ticket aggregator and filter for runtimes ≤ 120 min.  
3. Confirm the exact runtime (most sites list it next to the title).  
4. Buy tickets online, arrive a few minutes early, and enjoy a short, quality film.

If you’d like me to help you locate a specific film’s runtime or suggest a particular genre, just let me know!
